title: Optimizam result
description: The outcome of solving a problem file. See docs/result-format.md.

version.description: Format version, "major.minor". This schema describes major version 1.

status.description: How the solve ended. locally_optimal and locally_infeasible were added in result format 1.1, for nonlinear problems.

objective_bound.description: Optional, only with status not_proven_optimal or locally_optimal: the best proven bound on the optimal objective value (an upper bound when maximizing, a lower bound when minimizing).

conflict.description: Optional, only with status infeasible (result format 1.2): why. Constraints that can't hold together given the variables' bounds and types, and variables whose own bounds or domain leave them no value. Without --explain only causes that can be read off the model are reported.

constraints.description: Constraint names, instances of indexed constraints written like "capacity[north]"; a constraint without a name is called by its place in the problem's list, counting from 0: "constraints[3]".

variables.description: Variables with no value left, written like "x" or "x[north,3]". Each is a cause by itself.

minimal.description: True if every member is needed: without any one of them the rest can hold.

unbounded.description: Optional, only with status unbounded (result format 1.2): the variables with an objective coefficient and no bound in the direction that improves the objective. One of them is usually missing a bound.

objective.description: Objective value of this solution. Present exactly when the problem's solve method is minimize or maximize.

variables.description: Every variable in the problem, by name. A scalar variable maps to its value; an indexed variable maps to a table nested one object level per index set, keyed by set element (integers written as strings), like parameter values. Values are numbers, or for symbolic set-valued variables (format 1.1) elements of their set.

value.description: A number, or an element of a symbolic set-valued variable's set.
